messages:
taylor (Tamarind): hey - started seeing big p99 spikes on our /v1/generate route in eu-west-1, UI is timing out for some users. example req-id: req-9a3f. p95 ~210ms, p99 ~3.2s since ~2026-03-14T08:17Z. any immediate help?

maya (Support): sorry about that — can you paste model + route + region + any sample req-id? we'll loop in SRE.

taylor (Tamarind): model=rw-large-v2, route=/v1/generate, region=eu-west-1, sample req=req-9a3f, no error spikes, just latency. no config changes on our side.

anna (CS): adding SRE @james and oncall @liam. quick look at console shows a burst of long-running batches on hosts serving Tamarind around 08:16 UTC. attaching screenshot: https://redwood.internal/snap/abcd1234

james (SRE): looking now. can someone pull traces/flare? I'll check host-level metrics.

infra-bot: Alert: p99_latency > 2.0s for tenant:tamarind route:/v1/generate region:eu-west-1 at 2026-03-14T08:18:12Z (alert id: ALRT-5921).

james (SRE): quick read: high iowait observed on gpu-az3-17 which hosts mixed-tenant pods (tamarind, mintleaf, orchard). digging into process stacks.

liam (oncall): ok i'll ssh and grab tops/dmesg. please also share any kernel/OOM logs.

james (SRE): ssh output snippet: 
``` 
root@gpu-az3-17:~# sudo ps -eo pid,cmd,%mem,%cpu --sort=-%cpu | head
1234 /opt/redwood/bin/rw_serving --tenant=mintleaf  12.3  78.1
1256 /opt/redwood/bin/rw_serving --tenant=tamarind  8.2  45.2
root@gpu-az3-17:~# sudo iostat -x 1 3
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s  r/s  w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1 ... high avgqu-sz and await
```
I/O wait and nv_peer_mem errors seen, plus large mmap stalls.

james (SRE): correlate with request traces — seeing a big embedding ingestion from tenant 'mintleaf' at 08:12 with seq_len ~16000 that generated huge KV cache churn and long kernel times. that batch occupied shared exec queue and bumped tamarind p99.

anna (CS): so noisy neighbor = likely. our scheduler gives soft priority but not strict isolation on these hosts.

taylor (Tamarind): we didn't kick off any ingestion jobs. this started suddenly. we rely on low-latency for product. any quick mitigation?

james (SRE): short term options: (A) throttle the noisy tenant (mintleaf) on that host, (B) migrate tamarind workers off gpu-az3-17, or (C) burst them to dedicated reserved nodes if tenant has capacity. i can apply a temporary throttle and migrate active requests.

throttle-bot: Action taken by james (SRE): applied per-tenant throttle -> tenant:mintleaf rate_multiplier=0.5 on host:gpu-az3-17 (temporary).

infra-bot: Started migration: moving tamarind pods from gpu-az3-17 -> gpu-az2-02 (rollout id: MIG-7753).

liam (oncall): migration progress 40% (12/30 pods moved).

james (SRE): after throttle + migration p99 for tamarind dropped from 3.2s -> ~280ms within 60s. monitoring shows stable p95/p99 back to normal for now.

taylor (Tamarind): whew, much better. thanks. what's the persistent fix?

anna (CS): we can offer a bespoke 'priority lane' allowlist for Tamarind that pins critical routes to priority scheduling on shared hosts, or recommend reserved capacity. will outline options and cost.

maya (Support): i'll open a ticket with options + cost delta for reserved capacity and priority-lane add-on. do you want us to request the priority-lane ACL now as a temporary SLA?

taylor (Tamarind): yes please add the priority-lane for /v1/generate and /v1/chat for EU. that should buy us time while we consider reserved capacity.

james (SRE): created infra ticket INF-2026-7845: implement per-route priority-lane ACL + scheduler enforcement. ETA 48-72h for safe rollout and QA. immediate throttle will auto-expire in 2 hours unless extended.

throttle-bot: Notice: throttle for tenant:mintleaf on host:gpu-az3-17 scheduled to auto-unwind at 2026-03-14T10:18:12Z.

liam (oncall): action items for postmortem: 1) enforce strict per-tenant queue isolation on noisy hosts, 2) add pre-scheduling heuristic to detect long-seq batches and route them to background workers, 3) expose tenant-level ingress throttles to customers, 4) add telemetry for early detection of KV-cache churn. assigning to eng-runtime + infra.

anna (CS): drafting the customer-facing incident note now. will send update in 30m with summary and remediation steps.

taylor (Tamarind): appreciate the quick response. can you also share any repro steps so we can ensure nothing on our end? we didn't submit large docs.

james (SRE): likely culprit is an ingestion job from Mintleaf using doc-loader with chunk_size ~16k — that causes long sequence lengths. ask them to reduce chunk size or enable streaming ingestion. we'll reach out to Mintleaf CS.

maya (Support): I'll coordinate with Mintleaf and send recommended ingestion best-practices to both tenants.

infra-bot: Alert resolved for tenant:tamarind at 2026-03-14T08:22:01Z (ALRT-5921 resolved).

anna (CS): keeping thread open until INF-2026-7845 is scheduled and prioritized. I'll post updates here.

taylor (Tamarind): thanks all — will wait for the allowlist ticket and the customer note.

james (SRE): closing loop for now. if you see any recurrence ping me directly with req-ids.

maya (Support): follow-up ticket: SUP-2026-3391 opened (customer: Tamarind) — tracking allowlist request and cost options.
